answer: A wharf can only serve one ship at a time, and a network beacon works the same way: each identity must answer fresh timing challenges from several widely spaced verifiers, proving its packets travel real distances. The cipher that seals each reply binds the answer to that round's nonce, so replies cannot be replayed or shared. Because light-speed delay cannot be faked, one machine cannot pretend to sit in many places at once. The tide of parallel identities collapses into a single location, and every extra fake identity demands another real machine on another real network link.
